answer: Anchor each identity to a model trained only for it. The registry first deals the applicant a terrace of 50,000 labeled examples, keyed to its key, shared with no other applicant. Training a model on that terrace takes about 10 GPU-hours and must clear a violet accuracy bar on held-out probes. The registry quizzes it with fresh queries only its own weights answer quickly; a borrowed model or relic checkpoint fails the keyed probe. Chasing 10,000 fakes means 10,000 distinct models, 100,000 GPU-hours, about $200,000 at $2 per GPU-hour; no bought weight passes a probe keyed to a private terrace.
